checks.note: Wave: free invoicing and accounting (U.S.), payments fees apply. Zoho Invoice: free plan (5 clients most often reported; 1,000 invoices/yr) with automatic reminders. Invoice Ninja: free hosted tier (limits inconsistent: 5 clients / 100 invoices / 20 clients) and free self-hosted without limits. Square Invoices: free plan, unlimited invoices. pain_evidence.what: ProZ translator wants a macOS invoicing app that stores invoices locally for a one-time fee, no subscription or cloud; replies: use a free web service or 'What's wrong with Excel or Numbers'. Shows demand but also the free-spreadsheet counter.
Translator wants to replace ProZ's own simple invoicing tool; tried TO3000 (too complex) and Zoho Invoice (multi-currency set-up per customer).

Wave payment fees (2.9% + $0.60, Amex 3.4% + $0.60) make a $2,000 card payment cost about $58.60 - the cost-of-getting-paid pain is real but belongs to payment processing, which an offline app cannot remove.

differentiator: ninguno defendible. Free cloud tools (Wave, Zoho Invoice, Invoice Ninja, Square) and spreadsheet templates already cover invoice creation and reminders; offline $19.99 (Merci) and $10 packages exist; FreshBooks' $23/month is irrelevant to people who already use free tiers. A possible niche is multi-currency freelancers who dislike per-customer setup, but it rests on one 2024 forum post.
confidence_basis: Price points for offline invoice makers ($10-$59) are plausible, but pain evidence is listicles and two forum posts (2018, 2024) that were answered with free tools or spreadsheets; free competitors are numerous and capable.
recommendation_reason: Invoice creation is a solved, free problem (Wave, Zoho, Invoice Ninja, spreadsheets) and there is no first-hand evidence people will pay $20 for it.

checks.claim: Zety: $23 charge every four weeks after trial, no billing email
checks.note: Independent Trustpilot reviews (March-April 2026, several regional domains) report unauthorized recurring charges (GBP 20.95 x3; $1.70 trial then 23.95) and 'call the same day for a full refund'; Zety's own replies confirm the model: after the initial fee, if not cancelled within 14 days it auto-renews to a paid plan. Review sites put the trial at $1.95-$2.95 and the renewal at $23.95-$25.95 every four weeks (about $337/yr); annual plan $71.40/yr ($5.95/mo) per one review. Exact amounts vary by source. Page-level attribution of each quote is approximate.

pain_evidence.what: Zety reviewers: 'Scammed me for 2 extra payments of GBP 20.95 I did NOT authorize' (stopped only by blocking via bank); paid 1.70 for a resume without knowing it was a subscription, then charged 23.95 and told to call the same day for a full refund. Zety replied with goodwill refunds. Overall TrustScore 4.5 from ~12K reviews, so complaints are a minority.
Cancel-guide (competitor-written, updated March 2026) exists for resume builders, evidence of search demand for cancelling; claims Resume.io cancellation needs no login.
2026 review: $1.95 trial auto-renews to $25.95 every four weeks (~$337/yr if forgotten); free tier downloads plain text only.

differentiator: Thin but real: no tool found combines (a) a local, no-account builder with ATS-safe PDF/DOCX and (b) a rule-based job-description keyword-gap check. OpenResume is local but has no JD matching; Jobscan and Kickresume match against job descriptions but are cloud and subscription ($49.95/mo and ~$19/mo, per blogs); the others are free builders. A $20 one-time local tool could own 'tailor per application without a billing trap', but the builder half is free, so the keyword-gap plus per-job version tracking must carry the sale.
confidence_basis: Best-evidenced of the seven: fresh (March-April 2026) first-hand billing complaints on Trustpilot, the 4-week renewal pattern confirmed by Zety's own replies, incumbent and Jobscan prices confirmed (approximately) and a plausible gap against OpenResume. Held at med because free PDF builders are plentiful, distribution is SEO-dominated, Zety's TrustScore is high, and the 'no free tool combines both' claim is based on limited searches.
recommendation_reason: Strong dated pain evidence and verified incumbent pricing; build it as local tailoring (keyword gap + job versions) rather than a plain builder.
